title: OracleZoom: On-Policy Self-Distillation Inspired Reference-Constrained Recursive Image Super Resolution
abstract: arXiv:2609.06490v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recursive Super-Resolution (SR) extends fixed-scale SR to extreme magnification by repeatedly feeding predictions back into the same model, analogous to zooming an image repeatedly. However, ground truth availability at every scale, especially at depth, remains challenging as the required source resolution grows geometrically, leaving deeper predictions unsupervised. We present OracleZoom, an on-policy distillation-inspired, reference-constrained framework that trains on its trajectory while carrying the last ground-truth evidence beyond the supervision boundary. Direct and cross-scale supervision constrain verifiable content, while a no-reference quality objective guides unresolved fine-scale detail. A KL-constrained pretrained latent prior limits quality-driven drift, while EMA consistency stabilizes the supervision boundary. Across seven datasets, OracleZoom achieves the state-of-the-art SR quality across zooming scales, averaging 0

translated_title: OracleZoom：基于在线策略自蒸馏启发的参考约束递归图像超分辨率
translated_abstract: 递归超分辨率（SR）通过将预测结果反复馈入同一模型，将固定尺度的超分辨率扩展到极端放大倍率，类似于反复缩放图像。然而，在每个尺度上获取真实标签数据仍然具有挑战性，尤其是在深层阶段，因为所需的源分辨率呈几何级数增长，导致更深层的预测缺乏监督。我们提出了OracleZoom，这是一个受在线策略蒸馏启发、参考约束的框架，它在自身轨迹上进行训练，同时将最后的真实标签证据延伸到监督边界之外。直接监督和跨尺度监督约束可验证的内容，而无参考质量目标则引导未解决的精细尺度细节。KL约束的预训练潜在先验限制了由质量驱动的漂移，而EMA一致性则稳定了监督边界。在七个数据集上，OracleZoom在各种缩放尺度上实现了最先进的超分辨率质量，平均0
tldr: OracleZoom提出了一种受自蒸馏启发、参考约束的递归图像超分辨率框架，通过直接与跨尺度监督、无参考质量目标、KL约束潜在先验和EMA一致性等技术，解决了深层递归缺乏真实标签监督的问题，在七个数据集上实现了极端放大倍率下最先进的超分辨率质量。
en_tdlr: OracleZoom is an on-policy self-distillation-inspired, reference-constrained recursive super-resolution framework that achieves state-of-the-art quality across extreme zooming scales on seven datasets by combining direct and cross-scale supervision, no-reference quality objectives, KL-constrained latent priors, and EMA consistency to address the lack of supervision at deeper recursion levels.
